title: Product of the Latest K Entries
statement:
Build a stream that accepts non-negative integers one at a time and can report the product of the most recent ones.

  • RecentProduct() creates an empty stream.
  • add(num) appends num to the end of the stream.
  • getProduct(k) returns the product of the last k numbers added. The stream always holds at least k numbers when this is called.

Every product of consecutive numbers in the stream fits in a 32-bit signed integer. Aim for O(1) per call.

Tests are written as a list of operations and their arguments; the first operation creates the stream. The expected output has one entry per operation (null where nothing is returned).

examples.why: The stream is 4, 0, 3, then 5, then 2. Any window that reaches back to the 0 has product 0; the last three (3, 5, 2) give 30.
A zero only matters to windows that include it. The last single number is just 7.

constraints: Every product of consecutive stream numbers fits in a 32-bit signed integer
hints: Multiplying the last k numbers each time costs O(k). What running value, like a running sum, could answer any k in one step?
Keep prefix products: the product of the last k numbers is the total product divided by the product before them. What does a zero do to that division?
On a zero, throw away the prefix list and start a new one. If k reaches back past the start of the current list, the window contains that zero and the answer is 0.

explain.intuition:
This is prefix sums with multiplication. If pre[i] is the product of the first i numbers, then the last k multiply to pre[n] / pre[n − k]. Two lookups and a division, whatever k is.

The catch is zero: once it is in the product, every later prefix is 0 and you cannot divide by it. But a zero also answers the question for you. Any window that includes it has product 0. So on a zero, reset the prefix list to [1]. Afterwards the list only covers the numbers since the most recent zero. If k is longer than that, the window reaches the zero and the answer is 0.
steps: Keep pre = [1]; pre[i] is the product of the first i numbers since the last zero.
getProduct(k): let m = pre.length − 1 (numbers since the last zero). If k > m, return 0.
pitfalls: Storing a zero in the prefix list. Every later prefix becomes 0, and the division turns into 0 / 0.
Off by one on the reset check: with m numbers since the zero, k = m is still zero-free and k = m + 1 is not.
Keeping prefixes from before the zero. They can grow past 32 bits, and in JavaScript past 2<sup>53</sup>, where the division is no longer exact.

solutions.title: Multiply the tail every time
solutions.idea: Store every number and multiply the last k on each query.

solutions.title: Prefix products that reset on zero
solutions.idea: Prefix products since the last zero; the answer is a division, or 0 when the window reaches back to the zero.

followups: Numbers can now be negative. Does anything change?
Products no longer fit in 64 bits. Answer modulo a prime instead. Why does division become a problem, and what replaces it?
